footnote: Source: Autonomy et al., UK pilot report, Feb 2023. Gomes et al., Jul 2024. One model per team: mixed schedules were one reason Magyar Telekom ended its trial. Images are AI-generated
notes: Department heads choose the model. Fridays off: the whole department is off on Friday, which suits teams that work closely together and deal little with outsiders, with one named contact on call. Staggered: each person takes a different weekday off so all five days are covered, the only option for customer support and operations. Nine days in two weeks: one day off every second week and about 7.1 hours on each of the other nine days, 64 hours over the fortnight, for delivery teams that cannot step away for a whole day. Among 44 UK pilot companies that answered, 32% gave everyone Friday off and 25% had no shared day off. In Portugal more than 60% of staff took a day off every two weeks, though that trial cut hours to 36, not 32. One model per team: Magyar Telekom found that running four-day and five-day schedules side by side made coordination hard, one of the reasons it ended its trial after 18 months.
